response.answer: For a company, the beneficial owner is defined as the natural person(s) who has a controlling ownership interest or exercises control through other means [rbi_kyc_2016::chunk_015]. samples.question: What additional checks and approval are required to open an account for a politically exposed person under RBI KYC?

response.answer: To open an account for a Politically Exposed Person (PEP), Regulated Entities (REs) must perform normal customer due diligence and fulfill the following additional requirements: (1) implement appropriate risk management systems to identify if a customer or beneficial owner is a PEP; (2) take reasonable measures to establish the source of funds or wealth; (3) obtain approval from senior management to open the account; and (4) subject the account to enhanced monitoring on an ongoing basis. These requirements also apply to family members or close associates of PEPs. If an existing customer or beneficial owner subsequently becomes a PEP, senior management approval is required to continue the business relationship.

samples.question: When may an MSME loan be restructured under RBI directions?

response.answer: Banks are required to follow debt restructuring guidelines for MSMEs as specified in the Master Circular on Prudential norms on Income Recognition, Asset Classification and Provisioning pertaining to Advances [1]. Additionally, banks must establish a Restructuring/Rehabilitation policy for the revival of potentially viable sick units or enterprises [1]. Under the Framework for Revival and Rehabilitation of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises, which applies to loan limits up to ₹25 crore, banks are instructed to identify incipient stress in an account before it becomes a Non-Performing Asset (NPA) by utilizing the Special Mention Account (SMA) category [2].
